note_on_method: Each venue page below rests on one City of Mesa page, named in its sources, plus the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. Where the City says nothing (parking at all three, surface at all three, lighting at two of the three) these pages say that it says nothing, rather than filling the space.

slots.description:
Twenty-one lighted pickleball courts, which is one of the largest counts at any single venue in this directory. The City lists them alongside sixteen lighted tennis courts and four sand volleyball courts, all open to the public and available for rental.

This is a staffed racquet-sports centre, not a park that happens to have lines painted on it. There is a pro shop, and the City's rules state that "Court fees must be paid inside pro shop before using the facility. Unauthorized use of the facility is considered trespassing." Non-marking shoes are required, and ball machines are for hire at $18.00 per hour.
slots.getting_there:
4125 E McKellips Rd, Mesa, AZ 85215, in north-east Mesa. The Census geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in Mesa city, Maricopa County. The City publishes a phone number for the Center directly, 480-644-3874, and an email address.

On parking the City says nothing at all: no lot, no space count, no fee. What it does make clear is that arriving here is not a walk-on. You check in at the front desk before your reservation, and you pay at the pro shop before you play.
slots.what_to_expect:
The Center's hours have a hole in the middle of the day. It is open 5:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. every day, and then again 5:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. On Saturday and Sunday it does not reopen at all.

The City warns that "Tournaments, league and lesson programming, special events, or maintenance may limit court space for the general public", so the published hours are an outer limit rather than a guarantee.

The courts are lit; that word is the City's own. What the City never says, here or anywhere in Mesa, is whether these courts are indoor or outdoor, so this site does not say either.

faqs.a: $9.00 per court per hour before 5 p.m. and $13.00 per court per hour after. Fees must be paid at the pro shop before you use the facility.

faqs.q: Can I book a court in advance?
faqs.a: Yes, online, up to two weeks ahead. For anything further out the City asks for a reservation request form. Check in at the front desk when you arrive to get your court number.

faqs.q: Is this the same place as Gene Autry Park?
faqs.a: The Center stands inside Gene Autry Park and shares its street address, 4125 E McKellips Rd, which is why the park is not listed separately here.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts in a City park in central Mesa, counted by the City in the plainest way it counts anything: its list of reservable spaces at this park reads "Pickleball Courts (4)", and the number in the bracket is the whole claim.

The courts sit on a busy municipal site rather than on their own. The same list offers lighted softball fields, three lighted tennis courts and four lighted sand volleyball courts, and the park's Features add a lighted basketball court, restrooms, picnic tables, a playground, an unpaved walking path and ramadas both reservable and not. It is a neighbourhood sports park with a pickleball allocation.
slots.getting_there:
710 S. Extension Rd., Mesa, AZ 85210. The Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in the incorporated place "Mesa city", Maricopa County, agreeing with the City on the postcode.

The City publishes nothing about parking here. The park has a softball complex, reservable ramadas and restrooms, which in practice implies somewhere to leave a car, but the City does not say so and this site does not turn an inference into a fact. The park is open sunrise to 10 p.m., "or as posted", which is the City's own qualification and worth taking literally at a site that hosts booked softball and volleyball.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts, open from sunrise until 10 p.m., in a park with a good deal else going on around them.

Whether the courts are lit is the open question here, and the answer is that Mesa has not given one. The City marks lighting by writing it into the name of the amenity, and this park's own list names lighted tennis courts, lighted softball fields, lighted sand volleyball courts and a lighted basketball court. The pickleball entry alone carries no such mark, while lit amenities sit directly above and below it. That is a strong hint and it is still only a hint, so lighting is left unverified. The City also never says whether these courts are indoor or outdoor.

faqs.a: The City publishes no price for these courts. It also never says they are free, so this site does not describe them as free, only as having no stated fee.
Yes. The courts are listed among the park's reservable spaces, and the City directs bookings to the Mesa Tennis & Pickleball Center rather than to the park itself.

slots.description:
One court, and the City of Mesa describes it more honestly than most operators describe anything: "Pickleball Court (1 lined court shared with basketball use, bring your own portable net)".

Every clause of that sentence is doing work. It is one court rather than an unspecified several. The lines are painted on a surface built for something else. The basketball use has not been retired to make room for them, so whether the court is available depends on who got there first. And no net is provided, which is the detail that decides whether a trip here is worth making at all.

The rest of the park is an ordinary and pleasant neighbourhood one: a lighted basketball court, a BBQ grill, horseshoes, picnic tables, a playground and a non-reservable ramada, open sunrise to 10 p.m.
slots.getting_there:
The City prints the address as 1635 N Gilbert Road, Mesa, AZ 85213. There is a wrinkle in that, and it is worth knowing before you post anything to it: the US Census address geocoder matches the same street address and returns postcode 85203. Both are tier-one government sources and they cannot both be right. This site publishes the Census postcode and records the disagreement here rather than quietly choosing one. The street address itself is not in doubt, and the geocoder places it in the incorporated place "Mesa city", Maricopa County.

On parking the City says nothing at all, as it does at every Mesa venue on this site.
slots.what_to_expect:
Bring a net. That is the first thing, it is the City's own instruction, and without one there is no pickleball to be had here regardless of what the lines say.

After that, expect a single court that is also a basketball court, in a park open sunrise to 10 p.m. If someone is shooting hoops, that is the court. The City publishes no fee, which is not the same as publishing that it is free.

The park's basketball court is explicitly labelled as lighted by the City. The pickleball entry, which describes the very same surface, carries no lighting label at all, so lighting here is recorded as unverified. Nor does the City say whether the court is indoor or outdoor.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Yes. The City states it directly: bring your own portable net. No net is provided at this court.

faqs.q: Why does the postcode here differ from the City's?
faqs.a: Because the two sources disagree. The City of Mesa prints 85213 for this park and the US Census address geocoder returns 85203 for the same street address. This site publishes the Census value and states the disagreement rather than hiding it.
